6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Much of Frame Job's editing is direct: you drag, click and pinch rather than choose a command. This page lists those gestures by where you make them, with the modifier keys that change them.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['The timeline', 'The preview canvas', 'The Media tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
12	  tools={['set_selection', 'set_playhead', 'move_clip', 'duplicate', 'add_track', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'rate_stretch', 'slip', 'roll', 'set_audio', 'add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_clip', 'set_scope', 'close_gap', 'set_marker', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'add_clip', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'import_media', 'open_project', 'set_video', 'set_shape', 'set_text']}
13	/>
14	
15	On the timeline and the canvas, every drag that changes the project is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it. A click that doesn't move anything adds no step.
16	
17	## Selecting on the timeline
18	
19	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
20	| --- | --- | --- |
21	| Click | A clip | Selects it alone. Clicking a clip that's already in a multi-selection keeps the selection, so you can drag it. |
22	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | A clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
23	| Click | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Deselects everything. |
24	| Drag | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Draws a marquee that selects every clip it touches. |
25	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag | The same places | Draws a marquee that adds to the selection. |
26	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click | A track header | Selects every clip on that track. |
27	
28	A marquee skips clips on locked tracks, but a click can still select one. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
29	
30	## Moving clips
31	
32	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
33	| --- | --- | --- |
34	| Drag | A clip | Moves the selected clips, in time and to other tracks. A selection across several tracks keeps its spacing. |
35	| Drag | Past the top or bottom track | Puts the clips on a new track: a new front track above the top, a new back track below the bottom. Clips on more than one track can only make a new back track. |
36	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip | Duplicates the clips and moves the copies. The whole selection is copied when the clip is in it. |
37	
38	The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, and the others keep their offsets. A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves by the same time. Drag that sound to another track and only the sound changes track.
39	
40	Dragging a clip onto its neighbour on the same track makes a Cross Dissolve across the overlap, within the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
41	
42	During a drag the clip skips positions the project won't allow and waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts. If the drop can't go where you let go, a ghost of the clip animates back to where it belongs. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
43	
44	## Trim, stretch, slip and roll
45	
46	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
47	| --- | --- | --- |
48	| Drag | A clip's edge | [Trims](/editing/trimming/) that edge. |
49	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip's end edge | [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/): changes the speed so the clip fills the new length. |
50	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's body | [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the source under the clip while the clip stays. |
51	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's edge | [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the cut between this clip and the clip touching it. |
52	
53	**Trim.** The edge zone is 7 pt wide, and the pointer turns into the resize cursor over it. A clip 21 pt wide or less is all body, so zoom in to trim it. A trim keeps at least one frame and stays within the source file. Dragging the edge of a clip's detached sound moves the sound alone and leaves its picture, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
54	
55	**Rate stretch** works only on a clip that plays a media file. On any other clip, and on a start edge, <kbd>⌥</kbd> trims as usual. Nothing happens past the speed limits of ×0.1 and ×1000, or under one frame, and Frame Job won't stretch a linked clip.
56	
57	**Slip** never snaps, moves a frame at a time and doesn't change the selection. A linked partner on an unlocked track slips with the clip.
58	
59	**Roll** does nothing where no clip touches that edge, so not over a gap or a transition. Each clip keeps at least one frame, and a roll snaps as a trim does.
60	
61	Clips on a locked track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled.
62	
63	## Fades and the volume line
64	
65	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
66	| --- | --- | --- |
67	| Drag | A fade handle | Sets that clip's audio [fade](/audio/fades/) in or out. |
68	| Drag | The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) on a clip | Changes the level at that point, in dB, shown beside the pointer. |
69	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | The volume line | Adds a volume point there as an action, then sets its level. |
70	
71	A fade handle is the small square at the top corner of a clip's audio area. It lands on whole frames, can't go past the clip's length and doesn't snap to clip edges. It doesn't work on a locked track.
72	
73	The volume line grabs within 3 pt and drags up and down only. Its scale runs from +30.1 dB at the top to −60 dB, and the very bottom is silence, shown as −∞ dB. Inside or after an action that animates volume, the drag edits that action's end. Anywhere else it edits the clip's volume.
74	
75	Adding a point beeps inside an action that also changes something else, and less than a frame after the previous action's end.
76	
77	Pressing on the line with <kbd>⇧</kbd> held, or double-clicking it, acts on the clip instead, so selecting, slipping and renaming still work there.
78	
79	## Action bands
80	
81	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
82	| --- | --- | --- |
83	| Click | An action band | Selects the clip and that action, and moves the playhead to the action's end. The Clip tab then edits the action's end values. |
84	| Drag | An action band | Moves the action in time, on whole frames. It stops at the next action and at the clip's own length. |
85	| Drag | The edge of a band, its outer 5 pt | Changes the action's start or length, keeping at least one frame. |
86	
87	<kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects the action. A band 15 pt wide or less has no edge zones and is all body.
88	
89	While you drag, a dashed ghost marks the old place and a readout shows the new times and offset, or the change in length in frames. An action with no length has no band on the timeline. On a locked track, a click on a band selects only the clip, and the band won't drag.
90	
91	The action lane in the Clip tab moves and resizes bands the same way, and its **Clip** chip deselects the action. There, an action with no length can be selected but not dragged. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
92	
93	## Double-clicks
94	
95	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
96	| --- | --- | --- |
97	| Double-click | A clip | Renames it in place. |
98	| Double-click | A nest clip | Goes inside the nest. To rename a nest clip, use <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>. |
99	| Double-click | An empty part of a lane | [Closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). It beeps when there's no gap. It doesn't work above or below the lanes, where no track is named. |
100	| Click | The breadcrumb in the corner, while a nest is open | Comes back out by one level. |
101	
102	## The ruler and markers
103	
104	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
105	| --- | --- | --- |
106	| Click or drag | The ruler | Moves the playhead and pauses, playing the sound under it in short grains. |
107	| Drag | A marker | Moves it. |
108	| Double-click | A marker | Renames it. <kbd>⎋</kbd> keeps the old name, and an empty name changes nothing. |
109	
110	The ruler is the only way to [hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/). The transport keys move the playhead in silence.
111	
112	A marker grabs within 6 pt of its line and snaps. It can't land on another marker's time, so a drop there leaves it at the last time it could take. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
113	
114	## Track headers
115	
116	| Gesture | What it does |
117	| --- | --- |
118	| Drag a header | Moves the track up or down the stack. |
119	| Double-click a header | Renames the track. |
120	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a header | Selects every clip on the track. |
121	| Click the eye | Hide Video. |
122	| Click the speaker | Mute Audio. |
123	| Click the lock | Lock Track. |
124	| Click the headphones | Solo. |
125	| Click the sliders | Opens the track's [mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). The sliders are lit when the track's volume or pan isn't at its default, or the track has a compressor or limiter. |
126	
127	Right-clicking a header gives you a menu. See [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/).
128	
129	## Snapping
130	
131	While [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) is on (<kbd>N</kbd>), moving, trimming, stretching and rolling clips, dragging a marker and scrubbing the ruler snap to clip edges, markers, the start and end of the timeline, the playhead and the in and out points. They snap within 8 points on screen at every zoom, and a guide line shows the snap, except on the ruler. A slip doesn't snap. Every edit lands on the frame grid either way.
132	
133	Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag to turn snapping off for that drag, even if you press it partway through. **View ▸ Snapping** stays as it was.
134	
135	## Zoom and scroll
136	
137	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
138	| --- | --- | --- |
139	| Pinch, or <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> with the scroll wheel | Anywhere on the timeline | Zooms around the pointer, keeping the time under it in place. |
140	| Scroll | Anywhere on the timeline | Scrolls. The track headers stay at the left and the ruler stays at the top. |
141	
142	The zoom runs from 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, and the default is 42. During playback the timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view.
143	
144	The timeline's zoom has no menu item or shortcut except <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, which fits the whole project. The timeline bar has its own zoom controls. See [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/).
145	
146	## Dragging media in
147	
148	| Drag | Drop on | What it does |
149	| --- | --- | --- |
150	| A row from the Media tab | A track | Places the clip at the drop point. A drop that breaks the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) doesn't go in, and a smaller overlap makes a Cross Dissolve. |
151	| <kbd>⌥</kbd> and a Media row | A track | [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/): makes room by pushing later clips along. |
152	| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> and a Media row | A track | [Overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/): replaces what's in the way. |
153	| A Media row | The preview canvas | Places the clip on a new top track at the playhead. |
154	| Files from the Finder | The Media tab | Adds them to the project. |
155	| Files from the Finder | Anywhere else in the window | Opens each one as its own document, the same as dropping it on the Dock icon. |
156	| Files from the Finder | The Welcome window | Opens each one as its own document. |
157	
158	Only the modifier keys you hold at the drop count.
159	
160	A LUT row in the Media tab doesn't drag. Apply a LUT with **Clip ▸ Look ▸** or the Color tab. A drag between two open projects does nothing.
161	
162	## Canvas: selecting and moving
163	
164	| Gesture | What it does |
165	| --- | --- |
166	| Click a clip | Selects the front-most visible clip there. |
167	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
168	| Click empty canvas | Deselects everything and leaves crop mode. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, it keeps the selection. |
169	| Drag a clip | Moves the selected clips by the same amount. |
170	
171	A press on a selected clip's handle takes the handle, even with another clip under it. Clips on locked tracks don't move and can't be clicked, and neither can clips on hidden tracks.
172	
173	A drag [snaps](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) to the canvas centre, edges and thirds and to other layers' edges and centres, within 8 points at any zoom, with guide lines. <kbd>N</kbd> turns this off, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> suspends it, even partway through a drag.
174	
175	When an action is selected, a drag sets the value at that action's end, not the clip's own value.
176	
177	To place a clip by the pixel, type its [position](/canvas/transform/#position).
178	
179	## Canvas: scale, rotate and crop
180	
181	| Gesture | What it does |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| Drag a corner or side handle | Scales, with the opposite handle pinned. Video, image, freeze frame, graphic and nest clips always scale uniformly. |
184	| <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a handle | Scales around the centre. |
185	| Drag the rotation handle | Rotates about the clip's uncropped centre. |
186	| <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you rotate | Snaps to 15° steps. |
187	| Drag a crop handle, in crop mode | Crops, without shifting what's left. A ghost shows the uncropped picture. |
188	| Double-click any clip other than text | Turns on [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). |
189	
190	A drag keeps scale between 0.01 and 10. A crop always leaves at least one source pixel.
191	
192	Shapes and text have handles of their own:
193	
194	- **On a shape,** <kbd>⇧</kbd> on a corner handle frees the aspect ratio, and a side handle changes only the width or the height. A drag keeps the box between 4 and 20,000 pixels.
195	- **On a text clip,** the left and right handles set the wrap width. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly.
196	
197	See [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
198	
199	## Canvas: endpoints, regions and text
200	
201	| Gesture | What it does |
202	| --- | --- |
203	| Drag a line or arrow endpoint | Moves that end of the [shape](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/). The box doesn't change. |
204	| Drag an [obscure](/effects/obscure/) region's centre grip | Moves that region. |
205	| Drag one of its eight handles | Resizes the region. <kbd>⌥</kbd> resizes it around its centre. |
206	| Double-click a text clip | [Edits the text in place](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/), with the text selected and in the clip's own font. |
207	
208	Each side of a region stays between 1 and 20,000 source pixels. The grips show only with exactly one unlocked clip selected, outside crop mode. A drag inside the region but away from the grips still moves the clip.
209	
210	The text editor stays upright on a rotated clip.
211	
212	## Canvas: zoom and pan
213	
214	| Gesture | What it does |
215	| --- | --- |
216	| Pinch, or <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> with the scroll wheel | Steps the canvas zoom through **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** and **200%**. |
217	| Scroll | Pans a canvas that's larger than the preview. It does nothing while the canvas fits. |
218	| Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag | Pans a zoomed canvas that's larger than the preview. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
219	
220	See [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
221	
222	## Color tab controls
223	
224	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a wheel, a strip or a curve point to move at a tenth of the speed.
225	
226	| Control | Gesture | What it does |
227	| --- | --- | --- |
228	| [Wheel](/color/wheels/) or strip | Double-click | Resets it. |
229	| Strip under a wheel | Press the knob | Grabs it. |
230	| Strip under a wheel | Press elsewhere | Jumps there. With <kbd>⌥</kbd>, it drags from the current value without jumping. |
231	| [Curve](/color/curves/) | Click or double-click an empty part of the plot | Adds a point and drags it. |
232	| Curve | <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag | Keeps the point on one axis, the one it moved most along after 4 pt of travel. |
233	| Curve | Double-click a point | Removes it. |
234	| Selected curve point | <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd> | Removes it. |
235	| Selected curve point | The arrow keys | Nudge it. A tone curve steps by 0.01, or 0.1 with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. A hue curve steps 1° across, or 10° with <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
236	| Selected curve point | <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Deselects it. |
237	| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) strip | Drag a knob | Sets that edge of the range. |
238	| Qualifier strip | Drag a square | Sets the softness. |
239	| Qualifier strip | Drag the body | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps around. |
240	| Qualifier strip | Double-click | Resets it. |
241	| [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) | Click a zoom cell | Changes its zoom, on the first click even when the window isn't active. |
242	
243	A curve holds up to 16 points and at least two, and it beeps past either limit. A point stays between its neighbours. Hovering over the plot shows the input and output at the pointer. To reset a whole curve, use the **Reset** item for its channel in the channel strip's menu. See [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/).
244	
245	A qualifier range that's switched off doesn't respond to a press.

17	## Buttons with no menu item
18	
19	Most buttons in the toolbar and the timeline bar repeat a menu item, and their tooltips give its shortcut. These have no menu item at all.
20	
21	| Button | Where | What it does |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| **Loop** | Toolbar, at the end of the transport buttons | Turns [looping](/timeline/loop/) on and off. Playback repeats the in/out range when one is set, otherwise the whole timeline. The button is dimmed while Loop is off. |
24	| **Zoom Out** and **Zoom In** (− and +) | Timeline bar | Zoom the [timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) out or in by a step. |
25	| **Timeline Zoom** slider | Timeline bar, between − and + | Sets the timeline zoom about the middle of the view. The slider is logarithmic, so the same distance always changes the zoom by the same ratio. |
26	| **Add Text** (**Aa**) | Timeline bar | Adds a text clip at the playhead, the same as <kbd>T</kbd>. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip). |
27	| **Add Shape** | Timeline bar | Opens the shape menu. See [Add Shape](#add-shape). |
28	
29	These have their own control, and do the same as a **View** menu item:
30	
31	| Button | Where | The same as |
32	| --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Fit Timeline** | Timeline bar, after + | **View ▸ Fit Timeline** (<kbd>⇧Z</kbd>) |
34	| **Snap** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Snapping** (<kbd>N</kbd>) |
35	| **S**, **M** and **L** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**: Small, Medium and Large tracks |
36	| Zoom popup: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Toolbar | The canvas zoom. **View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** move through the same four steps. |
37	| **Safe** | Toolbar | **View ▸ Safe Areas** |
38	
39	## Add Shape
40	
41	The **Add Shape** button in the timeline bar is the only way to choose a shape to add. There's no menu bar item for it. **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color** also makes a shape clip, but only a white rectangle the canvas's size.
42	
43	<Steps>
44	
45	1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
46	2. Click **Add Shape**.
47	3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.
48	
49	</Steps>
50	
51	The shape goes on the front track at the playhead. If it doesn't fit there, Frame Job adds a new track above everything and puts it on that. The new clip is selected, and the undo step names the shape, for example **Add Ellipse**. See [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/).
52	
53	## Context menus
54	
55	Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click opens a menu in four places in the editor:
56	
57	- [A track's header, or the empty part of its lane](#track-header-or-empty-lane)
58	- [A row in the Media tab](#media-row)
59	- [A row in the inspector](#inspector-row)
60	- [A channel in the Color tab's curves strip](#curves-channel-strip)
61	
62	A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the timeline's corner opens no menu.
63	
64	A menu acts on what you clicked, not on the selection or the current track.
65	
66	While you record, the [recording status item](#recording-status-item) in the macOS menu bar has a menu too, and a plain click opens it.
67	
68	### Track header or empty lane
69	
70	Right-click a track's header, one of the buttons on it, or the empty part of its lane. The menu is for that track, and its checkmarks show that track's own state.
71	
72	| Item | What it does | Undo step |
73	| --- | --- | --- |
74	| **Hide Video** | Turns the track's picture off or on. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). | Hide Track |
75	| **Mute Audio** | Turns the track's sound off or on. | Mute Track |
76	| **Lock Track** | Locks or unlocks the track. | Lock Track |
77	| **Solo** | Solos the track, or stops soloing it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). | Solo Track |
78	| **Mix…** | Opens the track's mix panel. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). | |
79	| **Matte ▸** | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**, with a checkmark on the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). | Track Matte |
80	| **Remove Track** | Removes the track. If it holds clips, Frame Job asks first and says how many go with it. Greyed when it's the only track. | Remove Track |
81	
82	**Remove Track** here is the way to delete one empty track that isn't the front-most one, because an empty track has no clip to select. **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** deletes every empty track at once.
83	
84	### Media row
85	
86	Right-click a row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). The menu acts on that file, whatever the list's selection is.
87	
88	| Item | What it does |
89	| --- | --- |
90	| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, pushing later clips along, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). |
91	| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, replacing what's in the way, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. |
92	| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips that use the file, scrolls to the first one and switches to the Clip tab. Greyed when no clip on the timeline itself uses the file, which includes a file no clip uses and one used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). |
93	| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder: the original, or the project's copy when there's no original. It beeps when it has neither. |
94	| **Relink…** | Points this entry at a file you choose. It takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and its audio, video and alpha flags. Frame Job won't relink to a file of another kind, and a clip past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/). |
95	| **Remove** | Removes the file from the project. An unused file goes at once. A used file asks first, and its clips go with it, including clips inside nests. When the file is a LUT, the clips using it keep their place and lose the look, and any file it converts loses its Camera Log. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |
96	
97	### Inspector row
98	
99	Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them. The menu shows only what applies to that row, and with nothing that applies there's no menu. A text field or a popup keeps its own menu.
100	
101	| Item | When it's there | What it does |
102	| --- | --- | --- |
103	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action. |
104	| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action. |
105	| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default. Greyed when it's already there. |
106	| **Set end value to default** | The row has a default and animates, and an action is selected | Takes the place of **Reset to default**, and sets the row's value at the action's end. Greyed when it's already there. |
107	
108	On a row the selected action changes, the ◆ in the left gutter turns into × when you hover over it. Click it to remove the row from the action, the same as **Remove from action N**. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
109	
110	### Curves channel strip
111	
112	Right-click a cell of the curve editor's channel strip in the Color tab. **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat** puts that one curve back to flat, and is greyed when it already is.
113	
114	### Recording status item
115	
116	This one is in the macOS menu bar, not the editor. While a recording runs its time shows there, and a click opens its menu:
117	
118	- **Recording keyboard shortcuts**, a dimmed row shown only while shortcuts are being recorded
119	- **Pause Recording**, or **Resume Recording** while paused
120	- **Stop Recording**
121	
122	Its tooltip says whether Frame Job is recording or paused. If you quit while a display or window recording is running with the recorder panel hidden, Frame Job opens this menu so you can stop it.
123	
124	If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **Pause Recording** still work. See [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/).
125

9	Settings holds what belongs to you and not to a project: how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, your Anthropic key and the assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region, and whether graphics render while you're idle.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"

14	  where="Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…"

Assistant has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field, Compact when context reaches 300,000 tokens ticked, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, and Save and Remove buttons. Transcription has an AssemblyAI API key field, Region set to United States, and Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page buttons. Playback has Background render ticked, starting after 5 seconds."

21	
22	## Opening Settings
23	
24	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.
25	
26	The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.
27	
28	There's no OK or Cancel. Every control saves as you use it, and a key saves when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.
29	
30	Other places send you here:
31	
32	- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
33	- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note above the buttons in the Generate Captions sheet, and the **Generate** button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you. If every file already has a transcript it can use, you don't need a key and there's no note.
34	- With no AssemblyAI key and no filler transcript to use, **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** is greyed, its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)", and its tooltip is that same sentence.
35	
36	[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.
37	
38	## The info buttons
39	
40	The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.
41	
42	- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
43	- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.
44	
45	VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.
46	
47	## MCP
48	
49	This section shows how an MCP client, such as Claude Code, reaches Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.
50	
51	Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.
52	
53	**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:
54	
55	```sh
56	claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
57	```
58	
59	The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."
60	
61	The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
62	
63	The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
64	
65	## Assistant
66	
67	This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
68	
69	| Control | What it does | Default |
70	| --- | --- | --- |
71	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
72	| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
73	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
74	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
75	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
76	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
77	
78	There's no **Verify** button here. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.
79	
80	**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.
81	
82	**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
83	
84	Compaction loses the frames the assistant rendered earlier, so it renders again when it needs to look. Each clearing also adds to your bill. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
85	
86	Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
87	
88	The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.
89	
90	## Transcription
91	
92	This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
93	
94	| Control | What it does | Default |
95	| --- | --- | --- |
96	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
97	| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
98	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
99	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
100	| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
101	| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |
102	
103	A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses. A stored region Frame Job doesn't recognise counts as United States.
104	
105	**Verify** checks a key you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:
106	
107	| The line says | What it means |
108	| --- | --- |
109	| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
110	| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
111	| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
112	| Any other sentence, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" or "No network connection" | The check failed, and the sentence says why. |
113	
114	Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.
115	
116	The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
117	
118	## Playback
119	
120	This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.
121	
122	| Control | What it does | Default |
123	| --- | --- | --- |
124	| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
125	| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |
126	
127	The box and the stepper save the moment you use them, and a typed number saves when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
128	
129	Anything you do in Frame Job stops the drawing at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.
130	
131	Background render never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
132	
133	## How the key fields behave
134	
135	The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.
136	
137	- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
138	- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".
139	
140	The line under the controls reports what happened:
141	
142	| The line says | What it means |
143	| --- | --- |
144	| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
145	| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
146	| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |
147	
148	[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.
149	
150	## Agents and Settings
151	
152	No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.
153	
154	An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use needs no key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

2	title: "What Frame Job remembers"
3	description: "Which view choices, pane sizes, sheets and panels reopen the way you left them, what starts fresh in each window, and where those choices are kept."
4	---
5	
6	Frame Job remembers some of your choices between launches, so the next window or sheet opens the way you left it. These are your choices on this Mac, not part of a project, so none of them travels with a `.framejob` package. The [Settings](/reference/settings/) window has its own page.
7	
8	## View choices
9	
10	The last choice you made, in any window, is what the next window opens with. These apply to every project.
11	
12	| Choice | Where | Options | Default |
13	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
14	| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, <kbd>N</kbd>, or **Snap** in the timeline bar | On, off | On |
15	| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or **Safe** in the toolbar | On, off | Off |
16	| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>), which reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown, hidden | Shown |
17	| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or **S**, **M** and **L** in the timeline bar | Small, Medium, Large | Medium |
18	| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full, Half, Quarter | Full |
19	
20	Preview quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/).
21	
22	Holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that's remembered.
23	
24	## Pane sizes
25	
26	Drag the divider above the timeline, or the one left of the inspector, and new windows open at that size.
27	
28	| Pane | Range | Default |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| Inspector width | 280 to 440 pt | 304 pt |
31	| Timeline height | 140 pt to 60% of the window | 300 pt |
32	
33	The canvas stays at least 380 pt wide, and the area above the timeline at least 220 pt tall.
34	
35	Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, or hiding and showing the inspector, changes neither saved size, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.
36	
37	## Preview Window frame
38	
39	**View ▸ Preview Window** (<kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>) opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. There's one saved frame for every project.
40	
41	With two projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved. Whether the window is open isn't remembered. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
42	
43	## Sheets
44	
45	These reopen on what you chose last time. Any sheet not listed here opens on its defaults every time.
46	
47	| Where | What's remembered | When it's saved |
48	| --- | --- | --- |
49	| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | **Engine:** (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), **Style:**, and the **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses** boxes | As you change each one |
50	| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with, except **Dynamic Range** | When you press **Export…** or **Add to Queue** |
51	| **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** | When you press **Zoom** |
52	| **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:** | When you press **Follow** |
53	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:**, shared with Follow Subject | When you press **Make** |
54	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | **Rate:**, **Shortest stretch:** and **Keep pitch** | When you press **Apply** |
55	| **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** | **Minimum shot:**, **Cut:**, **Crosstalk:** and **Ignore bleed:** | When you press **Switch** |
56	| The **Normalize** row of the [Volume section](/audio/normalize/) | Its mode, **Peak** or **Loudness**, and its target in LUFS | As you change each one |
57	| The Document tab's **Canvas** section | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with your next [canvas-size](/projects/canvas-size/) change | As you tick it |
58	
59	Where a choice is saved on a press, cancelling the sheet saves nothing.
60	
61	The first time you export, the sheet opens on H.264 at document size. Named export presets are kept in a file, so they're on [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).
62	
63	**Follow:** can read differently in the two sheets that share it. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, it opens on **Speaker** again, and Follow Subject, which has no such choice, opens on **Subject**.
64	
65	**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference, not an edit, so undo doesn't reach it.
66	
67	No agent tool reads any of these. An agent's call uses the values it passes, or the tool's own defaults.
68	
69	## Recorder panel
70	
71	**File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) reopens on your last choices, each saved as you change it.
72	
73	| Group | What's remembered |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| Source | The display in **Source:**, **Include Frame Job windows** |
76	| Camera | **Camera:** and **Format:**, **Record the camera too**, **Layout:**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands** |
77	| Sound | **Microphone:**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **System Audio:** |
78	| Pointer and keys | **Cursor:**, **Show Clicks:**, **Record shortcuts** |
79	| When it lands | **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts**, **Speed up typing** |
80	| Picture | **Rate:**, **Size:** |
81	
82	Until you change them, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are off, **Zoom in on clicks** and **Show shortcuts** are on, **Layout:** is **Corner**, and **Cursor:** follows the default for the source.
83	
84	A few things don't last between launches:
85	
86	- **Record Into:** is never remembered.
87	- A picked window, **Microphone Only** and **Camera** as the **Source:** row last for the session only. The camera you chose is remembered, even though the row isn't.
88	
89	See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
90	
91	## Inspector sections
92	
93	Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, section by section, in every window. Only a click on a section's header is remembered.
94	
95	A section you've never clicked opens in its default state. Transform, a text or shape's main section, a graphic's Properties, and the sections of the Media and Document tabs start open, and most others start closed. If that would leave a Clip tab with every section shut, the first one you've never clicked opens. See [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).
96	
97	## Permission questions
98	
99	macOS shows its Screen Recording prompt only once, so Frame Job remembers that it has already asked. A later press of **Record** without the permission opens the Screen Recording pane of System Settings instead of the prompt. Input Monitoring, which **Record shortcuts** needs, is remembered the same way. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
100	
101	## Convert on import
102	
103	When macOS can't open a file and Frame Job offers to repackage or convert it, ticking **Do this automatically from now on** in that alert remembers your answer:
104	
105	- Ticked with **Convert** or **Repackage**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
106	- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails.
107	
108	There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
109	
110	```sh
111	defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
112	```
113	
114	See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
115	
116	## Update checks
117	
118	The downloaded copy of Frame Job remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).
119	
120	## What is not remembered
121	
122	**View ▸ Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** all start off in each new window. None of them changes an export.
123	
124	Nothing about the scopes is kept: a new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. The Loudness Meter starts off and empty.
125	
126	Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead, the selection and the in/out range aren't remembered between launches.
127	
128	Some rows in the sheets above are never remembered, even though the rows around them are:
129	
130	- **Zoom:** in Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version
131	- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
132	- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
133	- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
134	- **Dynamic Range** in Export
135	- **Minimum shot:** in Switch by Speaker when the cameras share one microphone
136	
137	**Clip ▸ Match Audio…** remembers none of its choices.
138	
139	## Where these are kept
140	
141	All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.
142

1	---
2	title: "Where Frame Job keeps its files"
3	description: "Find your API keys, spend ledger, export presets, converted movies, recordings and projects on your Mac, and see how Frame Job protects your keys."
4	---
5	
6	Frame Job keeps its own data in one folder in your Library and your recordings in your Movies folder. Projects live wherever you save them. Use this page when you want to back something up, clear something out, or check what's stored on your Mac.
7	
8	## What's where
9	
10	In this table, `…/Frame Job/` is short for `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.
11	
12	| Path | What it is |
13	| --- | --- |
14	| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your [AssemblyAI key](#key-files) |
15	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your [Anthropic key](#key-files) |
16	| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](#the-spend-ledger) |
17	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The Assistant's [cached price table](#the-spend-ledger) |
18	| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your [named export presets](#export-presets) |
19	| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | [Movies Frame Job copied or converted](#rewrapped-copies) from files macOS could not open |
20	| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The [local socket](#the-agent-socket) AI agents connect through |
21	| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | [Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs](#recordings) |
22	| Wherever you save them | [Projects](#projects), as `.framejob` packages |
23	| The `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain | [View settings and other remembered choices](#preferences) |
24	| macOS's temporary folder | [Files Frame Job can make again](#temporary-files) |
25	
26	## The Application Support folder
27	
28	Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The Finder hides your Library, so to open it choose **Go ▸ Go to Folder…** in the Finder and paste the path.
29	
30	Frame Job makes the folder when something first needs it, and each folder under it only when there's something to put there. You won't find empty folders for features you've never used.
31	
32	Each folder it makes has mode `0700`, so only your user account can open it. If you've already set a folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them alone.
33	
34	## Key files
35	
36	Your keys are two files in that folder:
37	
38	| File | What it holds |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| `assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key, for cloud transcription. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/). |
41	| `anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key, for the Assistant. It goes to the Assistant's helper, the background program that talks to Anthropic, when a conversation starts, and nowhere else. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/). |
42	
43	Save, replace and remove keys in [Settings](/reference/settings/). A file that's empty, or holds only spaces, counts as no key.
44	
45	## How keys are stored
46	
47	Each key is a plain file that only your user account can read or write (mode `0600`). It's written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written.
48	
49	A key is never:
50	
51	- put in macOS preferences
52	- logged
53	- passed as a launch argument
54	- passed to an agent tool, or returned by one
55	- shown in the Settings window again
56	
57	:::caution
58	Frame Job doesn't use the Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so treat your Mac account as the protection.
59	:::
60	
61	## Keys from the environment
62	
63	If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable. This only helps when you start Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable, because an app opened from the Finder or the Dock doesn't see your shell's variables.
64	
65	| Key | Variable |
66	| --- | --- |
67	| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
68	| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |
69	
70	- A stored key always wins over the variable.
71	- An empty variable counts as no key.
72	- **Verify** in Settings' Transcription section checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored. The Assistant section has no **Verify**.
73	- A key from a variable isn't stored, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.
74	
75	## The spend ledger
76	
77	`spend.jsonl` records one line per Assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. A response that was cut short is marked as one. The file never holds your key or the conversation, and only your user account can read it.
78	
79	The month's spend in Settings is added up from this file. If Frame Job can't write to it, the conversation carries on and the transcript shows a note saying why.
80	
81	`anthropic-prices.json` is the Assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. It's refreshed at most once a day. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
82	
83	## Export presets
84	
85	Your named export presets are in `ExportPresets.json`. If that file is missing or damaged, the presets list is empty and nothing else is affected. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).
86	
87	## Rewrapped copies
88	
89	The `Rewrapped/` folder holds movies Frame Job made from files macOS could not open: [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Your originals stay where they are.
90	
91	A project refers to the file in this folder, not to the original. If Frame Job can't find that file, the media is missing until you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) it.
92	
93	Every project shares this folder, and the only thing Frame Job deletes from it is a copy that turns out not to open, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:
94	
95	- WebM and MKV copies are made again from the original the next time a project using them opens, as long as the original is still there.
96	- ffmpeg conversions aren't. That media stays missing until you relink it.
97	
98	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies a project's rewrapped files into its package, which frees that project from this folder.
99	
100	## The agent socket
101	
102	An AI agent outside Frame Job reaches it through an MCP client, and that client connects through `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, a local socket Frame Job creates at every launch. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).
103	
104	## Recordings
105	
106	Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time: `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33`, or `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. The folder is made when a recording first has something to put in it.
107	
108	See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/) for every file a recording writes.
109	
110	## Projects
111	
112	A project is a `.framejob` package, saved wherever you choose. Each package holds its own caches, so they move with it. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
113	
114	## Preferences
115	
116	View settings and other remembered choices are in the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain. Keys are never stored there. See [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/).
117	
118	## Temporary files
119	
120	Files Frame Job can always make again go in macOS's temporary folder, outside any project: the caches of a project you haven't saved yet, and the [48 kHz copies](/reference/file-formats/#any-sample-rate) of sound at other sample rates. You don't need to keep them.
121	
122	## Related
123

125	- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
126	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
127	- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

2	title: "Supported file formats"
3	description: "Check which movies, sound files, pictures and LUTs Frame Job can bring in, what happens to transparency, rotation and odd frame rates, and which way in takes which file."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
12	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
13	  where="Drag to the Media tab"
14	  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions']}
15	/>
16	
17	## What Frame Job reads
18	
19	| Kind | Files |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
22	| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
23	| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
24	| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
25	| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |
26	
27	Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
28	
29	## Movies
30	
31	Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
32	
33	| Video | What Frame Job does |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
36	| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, using the decoder that comes with macOS. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
37	| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
38	| VP8 | Doesn't import. |
39	
40	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
41	
42	The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
43	
44	If macOS can't open the file at all and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can [repackage or convert it](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) on import.
45	
46	### Movies with alpha
47	
48	Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
49	
50	A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
51	
52	### Portrait and rotated movies
53	
54	A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
55	
56	### Variable and unusual frame rates
57	
58	Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track. A variable-rate file gets a single rate this way too.
59	
60	A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
61	
62	If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.
63	
64	## WebM and Matroska
65	
66	macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
67	
68	Add or open one as you would any other movie. A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
69	
70	## Sound
71	
72	M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
73	
74	### Any sample rate
75	
76	Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.
77	
78	### MP3 gapless start
79	
80	Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
81	
82	This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
83	
84	## Pictures
85	
86	PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
87	
88	A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
89	
90	Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
91	
92	### Deep and HDR stills
93	
94	| The still is | What Frame Job does |
95	| --- | --- |
96	| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
97	| Labelled HLG or PQ | Reads it as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, not as SDR. PNG and HEIC keep their colour space and depth. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
98	| Carrying an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's), as an iPhone HDR photo does | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
99	
100	A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
101	
102	## LUTs
103	
104	Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
105	
106	- 3D only. A 1D LUT won't import.
107	- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
108	- At most 32 MiB.
109	
110	A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.
111	
112	## Caption files
113	
114	An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
115	
116	Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
117	
118	## Which way in
119	
120	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
121	
122	| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
123	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
124	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
125	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
126	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
127	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
128	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
129	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
130	
131	A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
132	
133	In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.
134

1	---
2	title: "The .framejob package"
3	description: "See what a saved project holds, which parts Frame Job can rebuild and which it can't, and what happens when you move or copy a package."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A Frame Job project is one `.framejob` package: a folder the Finder shows as one file. It holds your edit, its caches and, if you ask for them, copies of your footage.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Consolidate Media…']}
12	  keys="⌘S"
13	  tools={['save_project', 'consolidate_media']}
14	/>
15	
16	## What a package is
17	
18	| Inside | What it is | Can Frame Job rebuild it? |
19	| --- | --- | --- |
20	| [`project.json`](#projectjson) | The edit itself | No. A package needs it to open. |
21	| [`cache/`](#cache) | Thumbnails, waveforms, analyses and renders | Yes, though [cloud transcripts](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) cost money. |
22	| [`media/`](#media) | Copies of your footage, only after **Consolidate Media…** | No. It may be the only copy. |
23	| [`graphics/`](#graphics) | Graphic modules, fonts, images and kept versions, only once you add a graphic, font or image | No. |
24	
25	To look inside, Control-click the package in the Finder and choose **Show Package Contents**.
26	
27	A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. A movie or a still is a separate step: see [Export](/export/formats/) and [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
28	
29	A save writes the new package beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave half a package.
30	
31	:::caution
32	A save keeps only those four things. Any other file you put inside a package is dropped at the next save, autosaves included.
33	:::
34	
35	## `project.json`
36	
37	This is the edit itself: the canvas, media list, tracks, clips and markers. It's the only thing a package needs in order to open.
38	
39	A project from any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format. A project from a newer build won't open, and the message asks you to update Frame Job. See [Open a project from another version](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-project-from-another-version).
40	
41	If `project.json` can't be read as text, the message says "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." See [When a project won't open](/projects/open-a-project/#when-a-project-wont-open).
42	
43	## `cache/`
44	
45	Everything here is something Frame Job can rebuild, so a package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and redraws.
46	
47	| Folder | What it holds |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `thumbs/` | Filmstrip thumbnails |
50	| `peaks/` | Waveforms |
51	| `loudness/` | Loudness measurements |
52	| `speech/` | Voice detection |
53	| `sync/` | The analysis for [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
54	| `transcripts/` | [Transcripts from AssemblyAI](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) |
55	| `device-transcripts/` | Words recognised on this Mac |
56	| `analysis/` | [On-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/): shot changes and sound events, faces and subjects found for an agent or drawn by **View ▸ Show Subjects**, and the masks made for an agent or for **Remove Background** |
57	| `reversed/` | [Reversed clips](/speed/reverse/) |
58	| `ramp-audio/` | Sound for [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/) |
59	| `isolated/` | [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) renders |
60	| `voiced/` | [Voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders |
61	
62	The per-file caches build in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. At most two files' sound caches build at a time. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Analyses and renders are made when something asks for them.
63	
64	Masks can make a package much larger, because they're kept for every frame: a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB.
65	
66	### Transcripts are worth keeping
67	
68	A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. Everything else in `cache/` rebuilds for nothing but time.
69	
70	## `media/`
71	
72	This folder exists only after [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/), and it holds copies of your footage. Unlike `cache/`, it may be the only copy, so don't delete it.
73	
74	By default a project doesn't copy your footage. It remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small but depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how a package comes to hold everything it needs.
75	
76	## `graphics/`
77	
78	This folder exists once you add a [graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), or a font or image for one. It holds the graphic modules, the small programs that draw each graphic, and these folders:
79	
80	| Folder | What it holds |
81	| --- | --- |
82	| `fonts/` | [Fonts](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
83	| `assets/` | [Images](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
84	| `history/` | The last 10 [kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions) of each module, one folder per module |
85	
86	## How a package travels
87	
88	Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder, and the first save copies them in.
89	
90	When you open a package, any media missing from its stored path is looked for in the package's own `media/` folder under the same name. That's what lets you move a consolidated package. A working link is never replaced this way.
91	
92	A referenced file that has moved is often found again through its bookmark. If it isn't, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
93	
94	To take a project to another Mac, run Consolidate Media first, so the footage goes with it.
95	
96	## Related
97

1	---
2	title: Limits
3	description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
4	---
5	
6	The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).
7	
8	## Project size
9	
10	| A project holds at most | |
11	| --- | --- |
12	| Clips | 4,096 |
13	| Tracks | 64 |
14	| Markers | 1,024 |
15	| Media files | 1,024 |
16	| Levels of nesting | 8 |
17	
18	Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.
19	
20	An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.
21	
22	A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.
23	
24	Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.
25	
26	## Canvas and layers
27	
28	| Limit | Value |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
31	| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
32	| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
33	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
34	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
35	| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
36	| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
37	| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |
38	
39	Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.
40	
41	Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
42	
43	## Timeline and editing
44	
45	| Limit | Value |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
48	| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
49	| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
50	| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |
51	
52	A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).
53	
54	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.
55	
56	## Speed
57	
58	| Limit | Value |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
61	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
62	| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
63	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
64	| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
65	
66	Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
67	
68	With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.
69	
70	## Audio
71	
72	| Limit | Value |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
75	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
76	| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
77	| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
78	| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |
79	
80	The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.
81	
82	A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.
83	
84	See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
85	
86	## Captions
87	
88	| Limit | Value |
89	| --- | --- |
90	| Longest file [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) takes | 10 hours |
91	| **Vocabulary** terms | 1,000 |
92	| [Caption import](/captions/import-captions/) | SubRip only |
93	
94	AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
95	
96	Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.
97	
98	A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
99	
100	## Colour
101	
102	| Limit | Value |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| Points on a [curve](/color/curves/) | 2 to 16 |
105	| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
106	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) override | 1 to 10,000 cd/m² |
107	| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |
108	
109	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.
110	
111	The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
112	
113	[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.
114	
115	## Export
116	
117	| Limit | Value |
118	| --- | --- |
119	| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
120	| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
121	| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
122	| [Master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
123	| [24-bit sound](/export/audio-only/) | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
124	| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |
125	
126	[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.
127	
128	On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.
129	
130	Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
131	
132	## Graphics
133	
134	| Limit | Value |
135	| --- | --- |
136	| Largest [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | 8,192 px on a side |
137	| [Property](/graphics/properties/) values on one clip | 64 |
138	| Options on one property | 32 |
139	| Characters in a string property | 4,096 |
140	| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |
141	| [Files watched for your saves](/graphics/edit-a-module/) | The first 16 module, font and picture files one by one, as well as the folders that hold them |
142	| [Memory for drawn frames](/graphics/playback-and-memory/) | A quarter of the Mac's memory |
143	
144	In a folder with more than 16 files, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
145	
146	## Recording
147	
148	| Limit | Value |
149	| --- | --- |
150	| [Camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) frame rate | One of the camera's formats, at that format's highest frame rate |
151	| [Camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) in the panel | Five. A corner layout is always the bottom-right one. |
152	| Length shown in the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) | Sized for up to 9:59:59. A longer recording shows a wider label. |
153	
154	There's no global shortcut to stop a recording, so use the menu-bar item or the **File** menu.
155	
156	If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).

158	## Assistant and agents
159	
160	| Limit | Value |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| [Compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) threshold | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens, 300,000 by default |
163	| **Clear old tool results** | Past 150,000 tokens, when it's ticked |
164	| Wait for a launched copy to be ready for calls | 60 seconds |
165	| Wait for `get_media_analysis` | 60 seconds |
166	
167	If Frame Job launches but isn't ready within 60 seconds, the call says so, and later calls in that client session don't launch another copy.
168
