1	---
2	title: "Where Frame Job keeps its files"
3	description: "Find your API keys, spend ledger, export presets, converted movies, recordings and projects on your Mac, and see how Frame Job protects your keys."
4	---
5	
6	Frame Job keeps its own data in one folder in your Library and your recordings in your Movies folder. Projects live wherever you save them. Use this page when you want to back something up, clear something out, or check what's stored on your Mac.
7	
8	## What's where
9	
10	In this table, `…/Frame Job/` is short for `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.
11	
12	| Path | What it is |
13	| --- | --- |
14	| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your [AssemblyAI key](#key-files) |
15	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your [Anthropic key](#key-files) |
16	| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](#the-spend-ledger) |
17	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The Assistant's [cached price table](#the-spend-ledger) |
18	| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your [named export presets](#export-presets) |
19	| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | [Movies Frame Job copied or converted](#rewrapped-copies) from files macOS could not open |
20	| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The [local socket](#the-agent-socket) AI agents connect through |
21	| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | [Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs](#recordings) |
22	| Wherever you save them | [Projects](#projects), as `.framejob` packages |
23	| The `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain | [View settings and other remembered choices](#preferences) |
24	| macOS's temporary folder | [Files Frame Job can make again](#temporary-files) |
25	
26	## The Application Support folder
27	
28	Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The Finder hides your Library, so to open it choose **Go ▸ Go to Folder…** in the Finder and paste the path.
29	
30	Frame Job makes the folder when something first needs it, and each folder under it only when there's something to put there. You won't find empty folders for features you've never used.
31	
32	Each folder it makes has mode `0700`, so only your user account can open it. If you've already set a folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them alone.
33	
34	## Key files
35	
36	Your keys are two files in that folder:
37	
38	| File | What it holds |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| `assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key, for cloud transcription. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/). |
41	| `anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key, for the Assistant. It goes to the Assistant's helper, the background program that talks to Anthropic, when a conversation starts, and nowhere else. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/). |
42	
43	Save, replace and remove keys in [Settings](/reference/settings/). A file that's empty, or holds only spaces, counts as no key.
44	
45	## How keys are stored
46	
47	Each key is a plain file that only your user account can read or write (mode `0600`). It's written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written.
48	
49	A key is never:
50	
51	- put in macOS preferences
52	- logged
53	- passed as a launch argument
54	- passed to an agent tool, or returned by one
55	- shown in the Settings window again
56	
57	:::caution
58	Frame Job doesn't use the Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so treat your Mac account as the protection.
59	:::
60	
61	## Keys from the environment
62	
63	If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable. This only helps when you start Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable, because an app opened from the Finder or the Dock doesn't see your shell's variables.
64	
65	| Key | Variable |
66	| --- | --- |
67	| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
68	| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |
69	
70	- A stored key always wins over the variable.
71	- An empty variable counts as no key.
72	- **Verify** in Settings' Transcription section checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored. The Assistant section has no **Verify**.
73	- A key from a variable isn't stored, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.
74	
75	## The spend ledger
76	
77	`spend.jsonl` records one line per Assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. A response that was cut short is marked as one. The file never holds your key or the conversation, and only your user account can read it.
78	
79	The month's spend in Settings is added up from this file. If Frame Job can't write to it, the conversation carries on and the transcript shows a note saying why.
80	
81	`anthropic-prices.json` is the Assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. It's refreshed at most once a day. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
82	
83	## Export presets
84	
85	Your named export presets are in `ExportPresets.json`. If that file is missing or damaged, the presets list is empty and nothing else is affected. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).
86	
87	## Rewrapped copies
88	
89	The `Rewrapped/` folder holds movies Frame Job made from files macOS could not open: [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Your originals stay where they are.
90	
91	A project refers to the file in this folder, not to the original. If Frame Job can't find that file, the media is missing until you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) it.
92	
93	Every project shares this folder, and the only thing Frame Job deletes from it is a copy that turns out not to open, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:
94	
95	- WebM and MKV copies are made again from the original the next time a project using them opens, as long as the original is still there.
96	- ffmpeg conversions aren't. That media stays missing until you relink it.
97	
98	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies a project's rewrapped files into its package, which frees that project from this folder.
99	
100	## The agent socket
101	
102	An AI agent outside Frame Job reaches it through an MCP client, and that client connects through `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, a local socket Frame Job creates at every launch. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).
103	
104	## Recordings
105	
106	Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time: `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33`, or `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. The folder is made when a recording first has something to put in it.
107	
108	See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/) for every file a recording writes.
109	
110	## Projects
111	
112	A project is a `.framejob` package, saved wherever you choose. Each package holds its own caches, so they move with it. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
113	
114	## Preferences
115	
116	View settings and other remembered choices are in the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain. Keys are never stored there. See [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/).
117	
118	## Temporary files
119	
120	Files Frame Job can always make again go in macOS's temporary folder, outside any project: the caches of a project you haven't saved yet, and the [48 kHz copies](/reference/file-formats/#any-sample-rate) of sound at other sample rates. You don't need to keep them.
121	
122	## Related
123

125	- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
126	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
127	- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

3	description: "Check which movies, sound files, pictures and LUTs Frame Job can bring in, what happens to transparency, rotation and odd frame rates, and which way in takes which file."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
12	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
13	  where="Drag to the Media tab"
14	  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions']}
15	/>
16	
17	## What Frame Job reads
18	
19	| Kind | Files |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
22	| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
23	| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
24	| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
25	| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |
26	
27	Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).
28	
29	## Movies
30	
31	Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:
32	
33	| Video | What Frame Job does |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
36	| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, using the decoder that comes with macOS. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
37	| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
38	| VP8 | Doesn't import. |
39	
40	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
41	
42	The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).
43	
44	If macOS can't open the file at all and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can [repackage or convert it](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) on import.
45	
46	### Movies with alpha
47	
48	Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.
49	
50	A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.
51	
52	### Portrait and rotated movies
53	
54	A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.
55	
56	### Variable and unusual frame rates
57	
58	Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track. A variable-rate file gets a single rate this way too.
59	
60	A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.
61	
62	If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.
63	
64	## WebM and Matroska
65	
66	macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.
67	
68	Add or open one as you would any other movie. A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
69	
70	## Sound
71	
72	M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
73	
74	### Any sample rate
75	
76	Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.
77	
78	### MP3 gapless start
79	
80	Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.
81	
82	This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.
83	
84	## Pictures
85	
86	PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.
87	
88	A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.
89	
90	Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.
91	
92	### Deep and HDR stills
93	
94	| The still is | What Frame Job does |
95	| --- | --- |
96	| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
97	| Labelled HLG or PQ | Reads it as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, not as SDR. PNG and HEIC keep their colour space and depth. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
98	| Carrying an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's), as an iPhone HDR photo does | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |
99	
100	A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). Animated GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.
101	
102	## LUTs
103	
104	Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).
105	
106	- 3D only. A 1D LUT won't import.
107	- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
108	- At most 32 MiB.
109	
110	A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.
111	
112	## Caption files
113	
114	An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).
115	
116	Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.
117	
118	## Which way in
119	
120	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.
121	
122	| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
123	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
124	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
125	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
126	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
127	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
128	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
129	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
130	
131	A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).
132	
133	In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.
134

1	---
2	title: "The .framejob package"
3	description: "See what a saved project holds, which parts Frame Job can rebuild and which it can't, and what happens when you move or copy a package."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A Frame Job project is one `.framejob` package: a folder the Finder shows as one file. It holds your edit, its caches and, if you ask for them, copies of your footage.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Consolidate Media…']}
12	  keys="⌘S"
13	  tools={['save_project', 'consolidate_media']}
14	/>
15	
16	## What a package is
17	
18	| Inside | What it is | Can Frame Job rebuild it? |
19	| --- | --- | --- |
20	| [`project.json`](#projectjson) | The edit itself | No. A package needs it to open. |
21	| [`cache/`](#cache) | Thumbnails, waveforms, analyses and renders | Yes, though [cloud transcripts](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) cost money. |
22	| [`media/`](#media) | Copies of your footage, only after **Consolidate Media…** | No. It may be the only copy. |
23	| [`graphics/`](#graphics) | Graphic modules, fonts, images and kept versions, only once you add a graphic, font or image | No. |
24	
25	To look inside, Control-click the package in the Finder and choose **Show Package Contents**.
26	
27	A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. A movie or a still is a separate step: see [Export](/export/formats/) and [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
28	
29	A save writes the new package beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave half a package.
30	
31	:::caution
32	A save keeps only those four things. Any other file you put inside a package is dropped at the next save, autosaves included.
33	:::
34	
35	## `project.json`
36	
37	This is the edit itself: the canvas, media list, tracks, clips and markers. It's the only thing a package needs in order to open.
38	
39	A project from any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format. A project from a newer build won't open, and the message asks you to update Frame Job. See [Open a project from another version](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-project-from-another-version).
40	
41	If `project.json` can't be read as text, the message says "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." See [When a project won't open](/projects/open-a-project/#when-a-project-wont-open).
42	
43	## `cache/`
44	
45	Everything here is something Frame Job can rebuild, so a package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and redraws.
46	
47	| Folder | What it holds |
48	| --- | --- |
49	| `thumbs/` | Filmstrip thumbnails |
50	| `peaks/` | Waveforms |
51	| `loudness/` | Loudness measurements |
52	| `speech/` | Voice detection |
53	| `sync/` | The analysis for [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
54	| `transcripts/` | [Transcripts from AssemblyAI](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) |
55	| `device-transcripts/` | Words recognised on this Mac |
56	| `analysis/` | [On-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/): shot changes and sound events, faces and subjects found for an agent or drawn by **View ▸ Show Subjects**, and the masks made for an agent or for **Remove Background** |
57	| `reversed/` | [Reversed clips](/speed/reverse/) |
58	| `ramp-audio/` | Sound for [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/) |
59	| `isolated/` | [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) renders |
60	| `voiced/` | [Voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders |
61	
62	The per-file caches build in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. At most two files' sound caches build at a time. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Analyses and renders are made when something asks for them.
63	
64	Masks can make a package much larger, because they're kept for every frame: a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB.
65	
66	### Transcripts are worth keeping
67	
68	A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. Everything else in `cache/` rebuilds for nothing but time.
69	
70	## `media/`
71	
72	This folder exists only after [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/), and it holds copies of your footage. Unlike `cache/`, it may be the only copy, so don't delete it.
73	
74	By default a project doesn't copy your footage. It remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small but depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how a package comes to hold everything it needs.
75	
76	## `graphics/`
77	
78	This folder exists once you add a [graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), or a font or image for one. It holds the graphic modules, the small programs that draw each graphic, and these folders:
79	
80	| Folder | What it holds |
81	| --- | --- |
82	| `fonts/` | [Fonts](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
83	| `assets/` | [Images](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
84	| `history/` | The last 10 [kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions) of each module, one folder per module |
85	
86	## How a package travels
87	
88	Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder, and the first save copies them in.
89	
90	When you open a package, any media missing from its stored path is looked for in the package's own `media/` folder under the same name. That's what lets you move a consolidated package. A working link is never replaced this way.
91	
92	A referenced file that has moved is often found again through its bookmark. If it isn't, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
93	
94	To take a project to another Mac, run Consolidate Media first, so the footage goes with it.
95

100	- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
101	- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

1	---
2	title: Limits
3	description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
4	---
5	
6	The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).
7	
8	## Project size
9	
10	| A project holds at most | |
11	| --- | --- |
12	| Clips | 4,096 |
13	| Tracks | 64 |
14	| Markers | 1,024 |
15	| Media files | 1,024 |
16	| Levels of nesting | 8 |
17	
18	Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.
19	
20	An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.
21	
22	A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.
23	
24	Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.
25	
26	## Canvas and layers
27	
28	| Limit | Value |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
31	| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
32	| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
33	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
34	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
35	| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
36	| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
37	| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |
38	
39	Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.
40	
41	Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
42	
43	## Timeline and editing
44	
45	| Limit | Value |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
48	| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
49	| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
50	| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |
51	
52	A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).
53	
54	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.
55	
56	## Speed
57	
58	| Limit | Value |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
61	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
62	| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
63	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
64	| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |
65	
66	Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
67	
68	With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.
69	
70	## Audio
71	
72	| Limit | Value |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
75	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
76	| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
77	| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
78	| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |
79	
80	The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.
81	
82	A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.
83	
84	See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
85	
86	## Captions
87	
88	| Limit | Value |
89	| --- | --- |
90	| Longest file [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) takes | 10 hours |
91	| **Vocabulary** terms | 1,000 |
92	| [Caption import](/captions/import-captions/) | SubRip only |
93	
94	AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
95	
96	Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.
97	
98	A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
99	
100	## Colour
101	
102	| Limit | Value |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| Points on a [curve](/color/curves/) | 2 to 16 |
105	| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
106	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) override | 1 to 10,000 cd/m² |
107	| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |
108	
109	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.
110	
111	The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.
112	
113	[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.
114	
115	## Export
116	
117	| Limit | Value |
118	| --- | --- |
119	| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
120	| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
121	| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
122	| [Master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
123	| [24-bit sound](/export/audio-only/) | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
124	| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |
125	
126	[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.
127	
128	On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.
129	
130	Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
131	
132	## Graphics
133	
134	| Limit | Value |
135	| --- | --- |
136	| Largest [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | 8,192 px on a side |
137	| [Property](/graphics/properties/) values on one clip | 64 |
138	| Options on one property | 32 |
139	| Characters in a string property | 4,096 |
140	| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |
141	| [Files watched for your saves](/graphics/edit-a-module/) | The first 16 module, font and picture files one by one, as well as the folders that hold them |
142	| [Memory for drawn frames](/graphics/playback-and-memory/) | A quarter of the Mac's memory |
143	
144	In a folder with more than 16 files, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
145	
146	## Recording
147	
148	| Limit | Value |
149	| --- | --- |
150	| [Camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) frame rate | One of the camera's formats, at that format's highest frame rate |
151	| [Camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) in the panel | Five. A corner layout is always the bottom-right one. |
152	| Length shown in the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) | Sized for up to 9:59:59. A longer recording shows a wider label. |
153	
154	There's no global shortcut to stop a recording, so use the menu-bar item or the **File** menu.
155	
156	If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).
157	
158	## Assistant and agents
159	
160	| Limit | Value |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| [Compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) threshold | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens, 300,000 by default |
163	| **Clear old tool results** | Past 150,000 tokens, when it's ticked |
164	| Wait for a launched copy to be ready for calls | 60 seconds |
165	| Wait for `get_media_analysis` | 60 seconds |
166	
167	If Frame Job launches but isn't ready within 60 seconds, the call says so, and later calls in that client session don't launch another copy.
168	
169	Agent calls run one at a time, and any call waits while you hold the mouse down mid-drag. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
170	
171	`get_media_analysis` keeps what it covered in its 60 seconds, then stops and says how much that was. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) for the Assistant's own limits.
172	
173	## Settings
174	
175	| Limit | Value |
176	| --- | --- |
177	| [Background render](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#set-how-long-it-waits)'s **Start after** | 1 to 60 seconds, 5 by default |
178	| Inspector width | 280 to 440 points |
179	| Timeline height | 140 points to 60 % of the window |
180	
181	[Converting on import](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. Frame Job looks on your `PATH`, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. For an install anywhere else, run this in Terminal:
182	
183	```sh
184	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
185	```
186	
187	`ffprobe` is taken from beside it, or else found by the same search.

1	---
2	title: Troubleshooting
3	description: Find out why a command is greyed, an edit is refused, a file won't open, a clip is silent or an export stops, and what to do next.
4	---
5	
6	Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).
7	
8	## A command is greyed out
9	
10	Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.
11	
12	If the item should be on, check these first:
13	
14	| Check | Why it matters |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
17	| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
18	| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
19	| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
20	| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |
21	
22	## A key does nothing
23	
24	Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.
25	
26	- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.
27	- **A sheet is open.** Close it first. In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the default button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.
28	
29	One more thing can catch you out: with a point selected on a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the clip.
30	
31	See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/) and [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).
32	
33	## An edit is refused
34	
35	When the project's rules won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the rule's own sentence appears at the foot of the inspector after "Refused: ":
36	
37	> Refused: clips 4 and 7 would overlap by 120000 ticks, more than half of the shorter clip (100000 ticks)
38	
39	The sentence stays until the project changes or you click it. It's exact rather than friendly. The clip numbers are Frame Job's own, not positions on the timeline, and a [tick](/reference/glossary/#projects-and-the-timeline) is 1/600,000 of a second. So this one says the overlap would be 0.2 s, and half of the shorter clip is 0.17 s.
40	
41	The rules you'll meet most:
42	
43	| Rule | What it means |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| The overlap rule | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. |
46	| A locked track | Its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and you can't insert onto it or close a gap on it. Unlock it with its [lock button](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
47	| The one-frame minimum | Trims and rolls leave a clip at least one frame long. |
48	| The ends of the file | A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. |
49	
50	Two other results look similar:
51	
52	- **A beep with no message** means the edit would have changed nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage. No rule was broken.
53	- **An error alert** means Frame Job couldn't use the request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range.
54	
55	During a drag, positions the rules won't allow are skipped, and the clip waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts.
56	
57	See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
58	
59	## A project won't open
60	
61	A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.
62	
63	| Message | What to do |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The project file inside the package is damaged. Open a backup copy if you have one. |
66	| "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it" | A newer Frame Job saved it. [Update Frame Job](/getting-started/updates/). |
67	| "too many clips: 5000 (max 4096)", or the same for tracks, markers or media | The file is past one of the [project limits](/reference/limits/#project-size). |
68	
69	Files that have moved don't stop a project opening, and neither does a damaged `cache/` folder. For moved files, see [Clips show a slate](#clips-show-a-slate). Also see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
70	
71	## A file won't import
72	
73	Frame Job tells you which file it couldn't add and why.
74	
75	| Message | What it means |
76	| --- | --- |
77	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | This Mac has no AV1 decoder. |
78	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | Only those two VP9 profiles import. |
79	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | This Mac has no decoder for that codec. Other codecs it can't decode get the same sentence with their own name. |
80	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
81	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
82	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because of a stalled network volume. |
83	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The message names the line of the file and what's wrong with it. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). |
84	| "Not enough free space to open *file*…" | A WebM or Matroska file needs room for its copy. The sentence says how much. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). |
85	
86	A file in a codec this Mac decodes still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
87	
88	If macOS can't open a file, you can repackage or convert it with your own ffmpeg. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
89	
90	If the **File ▸ Add Media…** panel won't let you choose a file, drop it on the Media tab instead. The panel lists only the common types. See [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
91	
92	An agent's `import_media` reports these reasons too.
93	
94	## Clips show a slate
95	
96	A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place and show a slate, and their rows in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wear the **missing** badge.
97	
98	When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once. Choose **Locate…** for a file, then **Relink**. Frame Job also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, so a shoot moved as one folder is usually found in one go. To relink a file later, use **Relink…** on its row in the Media tab. An agent uses `relink_media`.
99	
100	Two other cases show a slate or leave media missing:
101	
102	- A reversed clip shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
103	- A movie that was moved out of Frame Job's [Rewrapped folder](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder), where its WebM, MKV and ffmpeg copies live, stays missing until you relink it.
104	
105	See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
106	
107	## A clip is silent
108	
109	Check these in order. A muted clip, a muted track and a track silenced by a solo all draw the waveform faded.
110	
111	| Check | What to do |
112	| --- | --- |
113	| The clip's own sound | The clip may be muted in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/), or its [sound turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). |
114	| The track's **Mute** | A muted track is silent. Mute wins over Solo, so a track that's muted and soloed stays silent. |
115	| **Solo** on another track | While any track is soloed, the others are silent, even if the soloed track has nothing on it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
116	| The clip's rate | Above ×12 a clip has no sound, and the Speed section says "Audio is silent above ×12". On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
117	| Whether its sound has rendered | A ramp's sound, and a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, is silent in the preview until its render finishes. A failed render stays failed until the clip's timing changes or you reopen Frame Job. |
118	| **Detach Audio** | After a detach, the picture clip's own sound is off, and the sound is on its linked clip. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
119	
120	If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.
121	
122	## An export won't start or stops
123	
124	An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.
125	
126	While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out. Add a clip first.
127	
128	"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.
129	
130	| What you see | What to do |
131	| --- | --- |
132	| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
133	| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
134	| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | Frame Job won't export a graphic that can't draw itself. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
135	| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
136	| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
137	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
138	
139	A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
140	
141	:::caution
142	Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
143	:::
144	
145	See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
146	
147	## A feature asks for a key
148	
149	Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.
150	
151	| Message | What to do |
152	| --- | --- |
153	| "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | Paste a key under **Transcription** in [Settings](/reference/settings/). |
154	| "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." | Paste a key under **Assistant** in Settings. |
155	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The key failed. Check it, and press **Verify** to test it. |
156	
157	A transcript made in one AssemblyAI region can't be seen from the other, so check **Region** too.
158	
159	An agent can't set a key, so a person has to. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
160	
161	## Recording won't start
162	
163	A recording needs macOS's permissions, and Frame Job asks for each one only when you press Record.
164	
165	- **Screen Recording** is at **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**. Once it's on, relaunch Frame Job, then press Record again. Later presses without it open that pane.
166	- **Microphone**, **Camera** and **Input Monitoring** are asked for only when the recording needs them.
167	- If you started Frame Job from a terminal or another app, macOS applies that app's permissions. The panel's note names the launching process and how to relaunch.
168	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
169	
170	An agent's `record_screen` never asks for a permission, so a person has to grant it first. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
171	
172	## An agent can't reach Frame Job
173	
174	Only programs running as you can connect, through the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the app.
175	
176	| What you see | What to do |
177	| --- | --- |
178	| The client can't start the helper after you moved Frame Job | In the **MCP** section of [Settings](/reference/settings/#mcp), press **Copy MCP Command** and register the new path. The path is the one you opened Settings from, and it doesn't follow the app. |
179	| "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." | The helper isn't in this copy. Use a complete copy of the app. |
180	| "Frame Job did not answer at…" | Frame Job launched but wasn't ready within 60 seconds. Later calls in that client session don't launch another copy, so quit the stray copy and try again. |
181	
182	See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,

  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),

  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).

  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`

  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one

  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
